title: fazer.ai WhatsApp session protocol v1
description: Canonical wire contract shared by the Go connector (native provider) and the Rails session layer (native + uazapi backends). Frames are validated after decoding: numeric fields are numbers here even though Redis stream fields are transported as strings.

address.description: A WhatsApp addressable entity. `id` never carries the @server suffix, the device or the agent part.

party.description: The human/business behind an address. At least one of phone or lid is always present.

connection_state.description: Shape persisted in channel_whatsapp.provider_connection by ConnectionStateWriter.

media_ref.description: How to fetch the bytes of an inbound media message. `connector_blob` and `url` are fetched over HTTP; `uazapi_message` needs a /message/download round trip.

width.description: picture width in pixels, for an image, a video or a sticker; both sides or neither

height.description: picture height in pixels, for an image, a video or a sticker; both sides or neither

waveform.description: voice note amplitudes, exactly 64 samples of 0-100

content_reaction.description: Outbound only. Inbound reactions arrive as the message.reaction event.

order.description: An order placed from a business's catalog. Amounts are integers in thousandths of the currency's unit. items comes from WhatsApp's catalog API and is absent when it did not answer. An item's price_1000 is absent when its scale could not be proved against total_1000.

title.description: the order's title as WhatsApp carried it, the seller account's name. WhatsApp does not show it on the card

status.description: WhatsApp's name, passed through: INQUIRY, ACCEPTED or DECLINED today

surface.description: WhatsApp's name, passed through: CATALOG today

seller.description: the seller account's address as the order names it, a number or a LID

image.description: the product's picture, a URL on WhatsApp's media host

content_rich.description: Interactive or templated card (template, buttons, list, interactive). Carries the rendered parts as the dashboard shows them; the message preview text is derived from those parts, not sent separately.

kind.description: template, interactive, buttons, list, flow or order

product.description: The catalog product a card of kind product is, the kind a product sent on its own arrives as. Present, possibly empty, on every such card (#426).

media.description: Media in the header of the card, if any.

order.description: The catalog order a card of kind order is about. It travels inside the card, not as content of its own, because a client refuses a content type it does not know.

product.description: A product from a business's catalog, as WhatsApp carries it in a message. Every field is what WhatsApp sent: one it left out is absent, never zero or a default. An empty object is a product WhatsApp sent nothing readable about, still shown as one (#426).

price_1000.description: in thousandths of the currency's unit

sale_price_1000.description: in thousandths of the currency's unit

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, as WhatsApp sent it

retailer_id.description: the business's own code for the product

url.description: the product's page, when the business filled it in

image_count.description: how many pictures the product has in the catalog

owner.description: the account whose catalog the product is from

thumbnail.description: inline preview of the product's picture, a data: URI

quoted_product.description: the catalog product the message quotes, which is what a question asked from a business's catalog does: quoted_id then names no message. Present, possibly empty, whenever the quote is a product (#426)

client_ref.description: echo correlation token for providers that cannot accept a caller-supplied id

raw.description: provider node, kept for the rich parser and for debugging

event_frame.description: One entry of wa:events:<shard>. seq is monotonic per (sid, epoch).

command_frame.description: One entry of wa:cmd:<sid> or wa:control. reply_to is the wa:reply:<id> list an RPC answer is pushed to. deadline and max_runtime_ms are two different requests: deadline says do not start this after that moment, max_runtime_ms says do not let it run longer than that once started. A command carrying both gets whichever runs out first.

event_session_offline_sync_preview.description: The server is about to replay what this session missed while it was down. Counts are the server's own, sent before the events themselves, so a reader can say how much is coming instead of watching the queue move on its own. The messages arrive afterwards as ordinary message.received.

event_session_offline_sync_completed.description: The replay is over. What did not arrive by now is not coming, so this is where a reader stops waiting.

event_history_sync.description: a batch of history, discriminated by kind; the only kind is messages

history_messages.description: one slice of one chat's history, oldest first; a chat whose history is longer than a slice arrives in several

sync.description: why the phone sent it: the dump a newly linked device receives, or the answer to history.request

name.description: the group's subject, when the phone sent one

exhausted.description: the phone has nothing older for this chat

event_group_activity.description: Groups with recent traffic; the handler soft-syncs each one instead of doing a full fetch.

sdp.description: The connector's WebRTC offer, for the browser to answer with call.accept. Present only on a session that asked for calls.answer, for a 1:1 voice call.
The connector's WebRTC answer to the browser's call.start offer.

image.description: base64 JPEG; null or absent removes the picture

call_media_stream.description: A media server that carries a call's voice instead of a browser: the connector dials this WebSocket and exchanges 16 kHz mono PCM with it in JSON text frames (start, answered, media, stop one way; media, clear, hangup the other).

sdp.description: The browser's WebRTC answer to the sdp of the call.offer.
The browser's WebRTC offer for the call.
